```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Papasouliotis_2022_evobrutinib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Papasouliotis_2022_evobrutinib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.13417> (open access)

Evobrutinib is an oral, covalent (irreversible) inhibitor of Bruton's tyrosine
kinase (BTK). Papasouliotis 2022 fitted a population PK model to plasma
concentrations from two phase I studies in healthy adults and a population PD
model to BTK occupancy (BTKO) measured in peripheral blood mononuclear cells,
then combined the two to simulate steady-state BTKO under alternative once-daily
(q.d.) and twice-daily (b.i.d.) regimens. The PK and BTKO models were estimated
sequentially but are used jointly for simulation, so they are packaged here as
one model with two endpoints: `Cc` (evobrutinib plasma concentration, ng/mL) and
`target` (fraction of unoccupied BTK relative to predose). The derived output
`btko = 1 - target` is the occupied fraction.

# Population

The PK analysis pooled 76 healthy adult participants (2326 plasma observations,
29% below the 0.600 ng/mL LLOQ and handled with the M3 method):

- Study MS200527_0017 Part A (n = 42; 7 Japanese and 7 non-Japanese per cohort):
  evobrutinib 25, 75 or 200 mg q.d. tablets for 6 days, fasted.
- Study MS200527_0017 Part B (n = 16; 8 Japanese, 8 non-Japanese): single 75 mg
  dose fed (low-fat meal) and fasted, two-period crossover.
- Study MS200527_0019 (n = 18): single 75 mg tablet dose fed (low-fat meal) and
  fasted, crossover.

The BTKO model used 441 observations from 41 Part A participants (14, 13 and 14
at 25, 75 and 200 mg). Baseline demographics (age, weight, sex) are not
tabulated in the paper; sex, weight, BMI, BSA, Japanese ethnicity, age and dose
were tested as covariates and none was retained. The only covariate in the
final model is prandial state. See Papasouliotis 2022 Methods "Study population"
and Table 1. The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Papasouliotis_2022_evobrutinib")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source in

collects them.

|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL/F) | log(273 L/h) | Table 2 |

| `lvp` (V3/F) | log(446 L) | Table 2 |
| `lka` (Ka) | log(0.784 1/h) | Table 2 |
| `ltlag` (ALAG) | log(0.235 h) | Table 2 |
| `ld1` (D1, fasted) | log(0.181 h) | Table 2 |
| `e_fed_fdepot` (Food on F1) | 1.49 | Table 2; Results "increased by 49%" |
| `e_fed_d1` (Food on D1) | 4.27, D1 x (1 + 4.27) | Table 2 and its footnote (D1 fed = 0.954 h) |
| `etalcl`, `etaltlag`, covariance | 0.0958, 0.156, 0.0558 | Table 2 |

| `kin = kout` (BTK_FU,0 = 1) | n/a | Methods, steady-state equation and text |

# Virtual cohorts

```{r cohort}
mod <- readModelDb("Papasouliotis_2022_evobrutinib")

# rxSetSeed() fixes rxode2's random stream per solver thread but not across
# thread counts, so every assertion below is written to hold for any cohort.
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20221213)

# One cohort = `n` subjects given `ndose` doses every `ii` hours, all records
# sharing one prandial state. Doses use rate = -2 so rxode2 applies the
# modelled zero-order input duration dur(depot). Observation rows sit on the
# `target` state (an ODE state that is also a declared endpoint); rxode2
# returns Cc and btko on every row.
make_cohort <- function(n, dose, fed, ndose, ii, obs_times, label, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dosing <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = seq(0, by = ii, length.out = ndose)) |>
    mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", rate = -2)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "target", rate = NA_real_)
  bind_rows(dosing, obs) |>
    mutate(FED = fed, treatment = label) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, rate, FED, treatment)
}
```

## Figure 2 cohorts (study design)

Part A: 25, 75 and 200 mg q.d. for 6 days, fasted, with dense PK on Days 1 and
6 and BTKO sampled through Day 12. Part B / Study 0019: a single 75 mg dose
with a low-fat meal.

```{r cohort-fig2}
n_arm <- 100
obs_partA <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), seq(120, 144, by = 0.25), seq(144, 264, by = 4))))
events_fig2 <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(n_arm, 25, 0, 6, 24, obs_partA, "25 mg q.d. fasted", 0L),
  make_cohort(n_arm, 75, 0, 6, 24, obs_partA, "75 mg q.d. fasted", n_arm),
  make_cohort(n_arm, 200, 0, 6, 24, obs_partA, "200 mg q.d. fasted", 2L * n_arm),
  make_cohort(n_arm, 75, 1, 1, 24, seq(0, 48, by = 0.25), "75 mg single dose fed", 3L * n_arm)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_fig2[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate-fig2}
sim_fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_fig2,
  keep = c("treatment"),
  useLinCmt = FALSE,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2: concentration-time profiles on Days 1 and 6

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
sim_fig2 |>
  filter(time <= 24 | (time >= 120 & time <= 144 & treatment != "75 mg single dose fed")) |>
  mutate(
    day = ifelse(time <= 24, "Day 1", "Day 6"),
    tday = ifelse(time <= 24, time, time - 120)
  ) |>
  group_by(treatment, day, tday) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tday, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.6, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_grid(day ~ treatment) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.05, 2000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Evobrutinib concentration (ng/mL)",
    title = "Simulated median and 90% interval; dashed line = LLOQ 0.6 ng/mL",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Papasouliotis 2022."
  )
```

The simulated medians reach about 30-50 ng/mL at 25 mg, 100-150 ng/mL at
75 mg and several hundred ng/mL at 200 mg within 1 h, and fall below the LLOQ by
12-24 h at 25 and 75 mg, as in Figure 2 of the paper. There is little
accumulation between Day 1 and Day 6, consistent with the short effective
half-life.

## BTK occupancy through Day 12 (Part A design)

```{r figure-btko, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim_fig2 |>
  filter(treatment != "75 mg single dose fed") |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(btko, 0.05), Q50 = median(btko), Q95 = quantile(btko, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (day)", y = "BTK occupancy (fraction)",
    title = "BTKO, 6 days of q.d. dosing then washout",
    caption = "Part A design (BTKO sampled to Day 12); the BTKO VPC itself is Figure S5 of Papasouliotis 2022."
  )
```

## Table 4: steady-state minimum BTKO by regimen

The paper simulated 1000 participants per regimen for 14 days and reported the
percentage whose minimum BTKO over the last 24 h exceeded 70%, 80%, 90% and
95%, without residual error. The same design is reproduced below with 200
participants per regimen (the package cap). BTKO depends on the PK only through
`Cc`, so only the typical PK-PD linkage and the PK and PD random effects
matter here.

```{r table-4}
n_t4 <- 200
doses <- c(25, 50, 75, 100, 200)
design_t4 <- tidyr::crossing(
  dose = doses, regimen = c("q.d.", "b.i.d."), fed = c(0, 1)
) |>
  mutate(k = row_number())
obs_ss <- seq(13 * 24, 14 * 24, by = 0.5)
events_t4 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(design_t4)), function(i) {
  d <- design_t4[i, ]
  ii <- if (d$regimen == "q.d.") 24 else 12
  make_cohort(
    n_t4, d$dose, d$fed, 14 * 24 / ii, ii, obs_ss,
    paste(d$dose, d$regimen, d$fed), (d$k - 1L) * n_t4
  )
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_t4[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_t4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_t4,
  keep = c("treatment"),
  sigma = NA, # no residual error, as in the paper
  useLinCmt = FALSE,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

min_btko <- sim_t4 |>
  group_by(treatment, id) |>
  summarise(min_btko = min(btko), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::separate(treatment, c("dose", "regimen", "fed"), sep = " ") |>
  mutate(dose = as.numeric(dose), prandial = ifelse(fed == "1", "Fed", "Fasted"))

thresholds <- c(0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95)
sim_pct <- tidyr::crossing(min_btko, threshold = thresholds) |>
  group_by(regimen, prandial, threshold, dose) |>
  summarise(sim = 100 * mean(min_btko >= threshold), .groups = "drop")

published_t4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~prandial, ~threshold, ~`25`, ~`50`, ~`75`, ~`100`, ~`200`,
  "q.d.", "Fasted", 0.70, 98, 100, 100, 100, 100,
  "q.d.", "Fasted", 0.80, 88, 97, 99, 99, 100,
  "q.d.", "Fasted", 0.90, 36, 59, 71, 77, 87,
  "q.d.", "Fasted", 0.95, 4, 13, 20, 24, 39,
  "q.d.", "Fed", 0.70, 99, 100, 100, 100, 100,
  "q.d.", "Fed", 0.80, 95, 99, 99, 99, 100,
  "q.d.", "Fed", 0.90, 54, 74, 82, 85, 92,
  "q.d.", "Fed", 0.95, 10, 22, 29, 34, 51,
  "b.i.d.", "Fasted", 0.70, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100,
  "b.i.d.", "Fasted", 0.80, 99, 100, 100, 100, 100,
  "b.i.d.", "Fasted", 0.90, 88, 97, 99, 100, 100,
  "b.i.d.", "Fasted", 0.95, 38, 68, 81, 86, 94,
  "b.i.d.", "Fed", 0.70, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100,
  "b.i.d.", "Fed", 0.80, 100, 100, 100, 100, 100,
  "b.i.d.", "Fed", 0.90, 96, 99, 100, 100, 100,
  "b.i.d.", "Fed", 0.95, 59, 85, 90, 93, 97
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`25`, `50`, `75`, `100`, `200`), names_to = "dose", values_to = "published") |>
  mutate(dose = as.numeric(dose))

t4_cmp <- inner_join(published_t4, sim_pct, by = c("regimen", "prandial", "threshold", "dose")) |>
  mutate(diff = sim - published)
stopifnot(nrow(t4_cmp) == 80)

t4_cmp |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.0f / %.0f", sim, published)) |>
  select(regimen, prandial, threshold, dose, cell) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = dose, values_from = cell) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Prandial state" = prandial, "BTKO threshold" = threshold,
    "25 mg" = `25`, "50 mg" = `50`, "75 mg" = `75`, "100 mg" = `100`, "200 mg" = `200`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Percentage of participants with minimum steady-state BTKO above each threshold: simulated (n = 200 per regimen) / published (Table 4, n = 1000).")
```

```{r table-4-check}
# Structural gate: a mis-transcribed kout, kirrev, CL/F or food effect moves
# whole rows of Table 4 by tens of percentage points. The cells near 0% or
# 100% carry little information, so the check is on the centre and a robust
# upper quantile of the absolute differences. With 200 subjects per regimen
# the binomial SE of a mid-range cell is about 3.5 percentage points.
t4_summary <- c(
  median_abs_diff = median(abs(t4_cmp$diff)),
  q90_abs_diff = unname(quantile(abs(t4_cmp$diff), 0.9)),
  max_abs_diff = max(abs(t4_cmp$diff))
)
t4_summary
stopifnot(
  t4_summary[["median_abs_diff"]] < 5,
  t4_summary[["q90_abs_diff"]] < 15
)
```

Across the 80 cells of Table 4 the median absolute difference between the
simulated and published percentages is
`r signif(t4_summary[["median_abs_diff"]], 2)` percentage points and the 90th
percentile is `r signif(t4_summary[["q90_abs_diff"]], 2)`. The remaining
differences are expected: the paper's simulation also included five correlations
of at least 30% between PK and BTKO random effects (largest 42%) whose values
are not reported, and its cohorts were five times larger.

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA on the Figure 2 cohorts: Day 1 (0-24 h) for every arm and the dosing
interval on Day 6 for the q.d. arms.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_fig2 |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 144) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events_fig2 |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

# Every interval row names its treatment: the single-dose fed arm has no Day 6.
qd_arms <- c("25 mg q.d. fasted", "75 mg q.d. fasted", "200 mg q.d. fasted")
intervals <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(treatment = c(qd_arms, "75 mg single dose fed"), start = 0, end = 24),
  data.frame(treatment = qd_arms, start = 120, end = 144)
) |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(treatment, start, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_tbl |>
  mutate(
    interval = ifelse(start == 0, "Day 1 (0-24 h)", "Day 6 (120-144 h)"),
    across(c(cmax, tmax, auclast), \(x) signif(x, 3))
  ) |>
  select(treatment, interval, cmax, tmax, auclast) |>
  rename(
    "Treatment" = treatment, "Interval" = interval,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters (n = 100 per arm).")
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Papasouliotis 2022 reports no NCA table. The closed form for a linear model is
that AUC from zero to infinity after a single oral dose equals F x Dose / (CL/F),
so for the typical participant it must be 75 / 273 x 1000 = 274.7 ng\*h/mL
fasted and 1.49 times that (409.3 ng\*h/mL) fed. A typical-value solve analysed
with PKNCA is compared against those closed-form values; this checks the
structural model, the mg -> ng/mL scaling and the food effect on F together.

```{r nca-compare}
# 120 h captures > 99.99% of AUC; a longer window reaches ~1e-13 ng/mL
# integrator noise, which PKNCA turns into a NaN AUC.
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(1, 75, 0, 1, 24, c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.1), seq(25, 120, by = 1)), "75 mg fasted", 0L),
  make_cohort(1, 75, 1, 1, 24, c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.1), seq(25, 120, by = 1)), "75 mg fed", 1L)
)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_typ, keep = c("treatment"),
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
  atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10, returnType = "data.frame"
)
typ_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  bind_rows(
    sim_typ |> select(id, time, Cc, treatment),
    sim_typ |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
  ) |> distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |> arrange(id, time),
  Cc ~ time | treatment + id
)
typ_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  ev_typ |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, treatment),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
typ_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  typ_conc, typ_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
))

closed_form <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = c("75 mg fasted", "75 mg fed"),
  aucinf.obs = 1000 * 75 * c(1, 1.49) / 273
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = typ_nca,
  reference = closed_form,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "aucinf.obs",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Typical-value PKNCA AUC0-inf vs. the closed form F x Dose / (CL/F). * differs by >20%.")

typ_auc <- as.data.frame(typ_nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(closed_form, by = "treatment")
# Same drawn parameters on both sides (typical values): the only difference is
# trapezoidal and extrapolation error, so a tight bound is correct.
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_auc$PPORRES / typ_auc$aucinf.obs - 1) < 0.02))
```

## BTK recovery half-life

The paper states that the irreversible binding model estimates a BTK recovery
half-life of 159 h. After the drug has washed out, `d(target)/dt = kout * (1 -
target)`, so occupancy decays as `exp(-kout * t)`. The typical-value washout
slope after the 200 mg single dose reproduces it.

```{r recovery}
ev_rec <- make_cohort(1, 200, 0, 1, 24, seq(0, 720, by = 4), "200 mg", 0L)
sim_rec <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ev_rec, omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
wash <- sim_rec |> filter(time >= 240, time <= 720)
fit <- lm(log(btko) ~ time, data = wash)
t_half_rec <- log(2) / -coef(fit)[["time"]]
t_half_rec
stopifnot(abs(t_half_rec - 159) < 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **PK-PD random-effect correlations not included.** The paper's steady-state
  simulations used five correlations of at least 30% (largest 42%) between PK
  and BTKO random effects, but their values and the parameter pairs are not
  reported. The packaged model treats the PK and BTKO etas as independent, which
  is the most likely source of the residual differences from Table 4.
- **`kout` units.** Table 3 prints the unit of `kout` as "L/h"; it is a
  first-order rate constant (1/h), as confirmed by the stated recovery half-life
  of 159 h (ln 2 / 0.00437 = 158.6 h).
- **Residual error scale.** Tables 2 and 3 report the additive and proportional
  residual errors without stating whether they are standard deviations or
  variances. They are encoded as standard deviations: the Results describe the
  proportional errors as 49% and 43%, and the PK additive term (0.214 ng/mL) is
  of the right size relative to the 0.600 ng/mL LLOQ.
- **Separate D1 etas per prandial state.** The model carried a distinct random
  effect on D1 for fed and fasted dosing within the same participant; Table 2
  reports the same variance (1.39) for both, encoded as two etas with that
  variance, selected by `FED`.
- **Food effects.** Bioavailability is 1 fasted and 1.49 fed
  (`e_fed_fdepot^FED`); D1 is 0.181 h fasted and 0.181 x (1 + 4.27) = 0.954 h
  fed, as stated in the Table 2 footnote. All fed data came from a low-fat meal;
  the paper describes the covariate generically as food state, so the general
  `FED` indicator is used.
- **BTKO baseline.** BTK occupancy data were baseline-corrected, so the
  fraction unoccupied starts at 1 and `kin = kout` (Methods). The observed
  endpoint is the fraction unoccupied (`target`); `btko = 1 - target`.
- **Covariate screen.** Sex, weight, BMI, BSA, Japanese versus non-Japanese
  ethnicity, age and dose were tested and not retained; they are listed in
  `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Cohort sizes.** Figure 2 cohorts use 100 participants per arm and the
  Table 4 replication 200 per regimen (the paper used 1000).
- Demographics (age, weight, sex) are not reported, so the virtual cohorts carry
  no demographic covariates; none enters the model.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found as of 2026-10-10.
